name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean makes a Democratic win structurally very difficult
Stigall's roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage over Smead
Polymarket prices the Republican near 95 percent
Open seat with no public polling adds residual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean, Stigall's roughly seven-to-one fundraising edge, and prediction markets near 95 percent Republican all point to a comfortable Republican hold despite Graves's retirement. Nothing in the money totals, outside spending, or environment suggests the race is competitive.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending surge putting Smead within single digits would signal an unexpected wave environment and warrant reevaluation.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Missouri's 6th District is a deeply Republican seat, and Sam Graves's retirement does not appear to change that. The Republican nominee, Chris Stigall, has raised roughly $969,000 to about $130,000 for Democrat Josh Smead, and outside groups have spent against Stigall without any evidence of a competitive race emerging. No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on the district's R+19 lean, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, where Polymarket prices the Republican near 95 percent.

A Democratic win would require a national swing far exceeding anything visible in current fundamentals. The Libertarian candidate adds a minor unknown but is not viewed as a factor. The forecast expects the Republican to carry the open seat by a wide, double-digit margin, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling in this rural northwest Missouri district.
